relations.subject: n1ql:indexing-metadata-fields
relations.evidence: Starting with Couchbase Server 8.0, you can index any number of XATTR fields using the [CREATE INDEX](createindex.md) statement.

relations.subject: n1ql:indexing-metadata-fields
relations.evidence: Value representing the current state of an item which changes every time the item is modified. For details, refer to [Concurrent Document Mutations](../../../java-sdk/current/howtos/concurrent-document-mutations.md).

relations.subject: n1ql:indexing-metadata-fields
relations.evidence: Value representing a document's expiration date. A value of 0 (zero) means no expiration date. For details, refer to [KV Operations](../../../java-sdk/current/howtos/kv-operations.md#document-expiration).

relations.subject: n1ql:indexing-metadata-fields
relations.evidence: To try the examples in this section, set the query context to the `inventory` scope in the travel sample dataset. For more information, see [Query Context](../n1ql-intro/queriesandresults.md#query-context).

notable_absence.finding: Same absence as server/'s version of this page: no Prerequisites/RBAC section, despite describing an enforced, consequential constraint ('If you attempt to build an index on a metadata field that's not indexable, an error is returned') and depending entirely on CREATE INDEX for privilege gating.

cross_component_finding: Links out to two java-sdk howto pages (Concurrent Document Mutations for `cas`, KV Operations#document-expiration for `expiration`) to explain the underlying semantics of the metadata fields it lets you index - the n1ql: statement-reference layer treats SDK-level concurrency/expiration semantics as out-of-scope background. Minted sdk:concurrent-document-mutations and sdk:document-expiration since neither existed; the document-expiration link recurs verbatim on insert.json in this same batch.
